file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

old_string.description: The text to replace (always sent together with new_string)

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string; required whenever old_string is sent — "" deletes the text)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurences of old_string (default false)

expected_anchor.description: The staleness anchor from your most recent Read of this file: the parenthesised "(anchor: …)" value, carried across exactly

hunks.description: Line-addressed hunks against the anchored snapshot. Mutually exclusive with old_string/new_string; requires expected_anchor unless every hunk is anchor-qualified ("12#ab3f" from a line_anchors read — then the line anchors are the staleness contract).

lines.description: A 1-based line number ("12"), inclusive range ("12-18"), or anchor-qualified spelling copied exactly from a line_anchors read ("12#ab3f", "12#ab3f-18#9c2e"); an anchored endpoint is checked against the current content, and a drifted line refuses with the current anchors — re-aim from those, never retype content.

replace.description: The replacement body ("" deletes the range; with insert, the inserted body)

insert.description: Insert relative to the single anchor line instead of replacing it

append.description: Text added at the end of the file on its own line (the file is created when absent), no prior read needed; with `section`, at the end of that section instead. Mutually exclusive with old_string/new_string/hunks.

section.description: A Markdown heading line exactly as it stands in the file ("## Checks"), which must occur once, naming the section (the heading through the line before the next heading of the same or a higher level): with new_string the whole section, heading included, becomes new_string; with append the text is added inside it. Mutually exclusive with old_string/hunks.

description: One of four shapes: old_string + new_string (both required together; replace_all rewrites every occurrence) · hunks · append · section + new_string
